lines.text: What if you woke up a thousand years in the future?
The pod hisses open. The lab is silent, and nobody is waiting for you.
You try to stand, and your legs give way.
Unused muscles waste away, so your first battle is just reaching the door.
Outside, a drone asks you something. You don't understand a single word.
The English of a thousand years ago is unreadable to us today. Now you're the one from the past.
Doors won't open for you. A food kiosk scans your face, and finds nothing.
No identity, no money, no record that you were ever born.
Then you start to cough. Germs have kept evolving for a thousand years.
Your immune system has never met them, and your old germs could be just as dangerous to them.
Night falls. You curl up under a bridge, as silent trains glide overhead.
Everything is cleaner, faster and brighter, and you have never felt more lost.
At dawn, a stranger stops. Her earpiece translates your ancient words.
She takes you to a clinic, and for the first time, someone says your name back to you.
To them, you're a living history book.
So, would you rather wake up in the future, or never wake up at all?
